articleTitle: Experimental implementations of priority inheritance semaphore on ITRON-specification kernel
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 11th TRON project International Symposium
abstract: Using priority inheritance protocols is an effective approach to solve the problem of uncontrolled priority inversion, which is among the major sources of deadline violations in hard real-time systems. In this paper, some approaches to incorporate priority inheritance to the ITRON specification are discussed. As the result, we propose two specifications of priority inheritance semaphore functions with which the basic priority inheritance protocol can be realized, and implement both of them for evaluation. The run-time performance and memory requirements of the functions are evaluated with the implementations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A 32-bit microprocessor with efficient testable designs, the TX2
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 11th TRON project International Symposium
abstract: A 32-bit microprocessor, the TX2, with efficient testable designs, has been developed. For manufacturing test, a combination of powerful BISTs and parallel scan design is implemented. The BISTs achieve 100% functional coverage for ROM, RAM and PLA and 78% coverage of single stuck-at faults of the remaining part of the TX2 including redundant faults. Scan test vectors obtained by ATPG have enhanced the coverage to 84%. Total test time is less than 2 seconds. There are also a few circuits for efficient design verification. Moreover, for higher test quality, Idd.q test is implemented. Total area overhead is 6.9%.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Expansion of CTRON interface for fault-tolerant system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 11th TRON project International Symposium
abstract: Nonstop systems such as switching systems and gateway systems must be "Realtime-Fault-Tolerant", with high real-time capability and high availability. The CTRON interface has been specified for real time communication processing. This paper considers the CTRON specification's adaptability to fault tolerant systems from the following point of view, and then clarifies some problems: management of device status; detection of changes in device configuration; relationship between failed physical devices and logical devices. Finally the authors propose nine new functions (system calls) and asynchronous report interfaces (message boxes) to solve the problems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Quantitative evaluation of the reliability benefits of maintenance bus implementation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 11th TRON project International Symposium
abstract: Among methods highly improving system reliability and maintainability is use of a dedicated route called maintenance bus for isolating and diagnosing devices. We have evaluated the reliability benefits of the system with maintenance bus. Our studies have yielded the following results: (a) when a periodically health-checked maintenance bus is used, the state probability where normal operation cannot be guaranteed is reduced on the order of three to four decimal places compared to a system without a separate maintenance bus, (b) immediate isolation and recovery procedure for a maintenance bus fault is preferable, and (c) a bit serial bus connection is the most reliable configuration. The TRON serial bus standard offers a promising alternative as a maintenance bus.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A 32-bit superscalar microprocessor G/sub MICRO//400 for embedded systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 11th TRON project International Symposium
abstract: This paper describes a 32-bit superscalar microprocessor G/sub MICRO//400, based on the TRON architecture specifications. The G/sub MICRO//400 has a dual issued instruction pipeline, a pre-jump mechanism and a high-speed memory access interface. To realize high performance in processing of series data such as frame buffer or character-strings, the G/sub MICRO//400 has improved the execution efficiency of multiple-operation instructions by block-data-transfer and 64-bit processing. In order to improve the task switching latency, the on-chip caches are used as a local memory in which the context blocks are stored. These techniques are suitable for realtime embedded systems, such as X-window terminals and printers. Using 0.5 /spl mu/m triple-layer metal CMOS technology, the G/sub MICRO//400 integrates 1485K transistors on a 108 mm/sup 2/ die area. The G/sub MICRO//400 achieves a processing speed of 45 MIPS at 40 MHz.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of a fault tolerant communication platform, the HPT500
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 11th TRON project International Symposium
abstract: The authors developed a high-reliability platform, the HPT500, with a realtime OS complying with the IROS specifications. The IROS specifications were defined by NTT based on the CTRON interface specifications. The HPT500 is provided with a hardware function that detects board unplugging/plugging in automatically. This function can automatically change the system configuration just by plugging in or unplugging a board (online extension/reduction). In addition, since the HPT500 supports the SNMP, a workstation can be used as the remote maintenance terminal to monitor and control the system visually in realtime.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: After a decade of TRON, what comes next?
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 11th TRON project International Symposium
abstract: The TRON("The Real-time Operating System Nucleus") Project is researching large-scale, highly functionally distributed systems for the "computing everywhere" environment of the 21st century, when computers will be used in practically every kind of object imaginable. The project started up officially in 1984. This paper looks at the background out of which the project emerged, and examines once again the aims and philosophy that guide it. It reviews what we have accomplished over the past decade, and looks ahead to future directions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fault-tolerant implementation of the CTRON basic operating system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 11th TRON project International Symposium
abstract: Tandem Computers has developed an operating system based on the CTRON specifications and implemented it on our fault-tolerant Integrity C series hardware platform (C/S2). This work has been done in conjunction with the Network Information Systems Laboratory of Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation (NTT). The current version of this operating system is presently being used in a production system within NTT. We are now working on enhancements to the system to adapt it to the latest hardware models in the Integrity Series. In this paper, we make a brief overview of our project and describe how we have integrated Tandem's fault-tolerant architecture for the Integrity Series with CTRON and its definitions for a common set of operating system interfaces. In implementing CTRON on our hardware fault-tolerant platform, one of our primary goals was to ensure that application programs did not have to be modified to accrue the advantages of fault-tolerant operation. CTRON interfaces are supported unchanged. Thus, application programs which adhere to specified CTRON interfaces will run unmodified in a fault-tolerant environment. No additional modifications to checkpoint state or effect process recovery are necessary at the application programming level to take full advantage of the fault-tolerant features of the system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of label metaphor using shared interaction object architecture
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 11th TRON project International Symposium
abstract: Label model is a framework of script processing, which is a natural extension of desktop metaphor like the BTRON GUI environment. The main idea of the label model is that a script program is just a piece of "memo label" attached upon a document, which contains several operations on the document. In the model, a script program is described as a sequence of operations on graphical objects of the document data. The main contribution of this paper is to demonstrate that shared interaction-object architecture facilitates the implementation of the label model. It is an architecture model of GUI applications, in which graphical objects of GUI applications are preserved in distributed shared memories specially tailored for GUI. This allows script programs to operate the data from outside the GUI applications. The major benefit of this architecture is that it satisfies the following two requirements: First, script processing can be handled transparently from GUI applications, second, this architecture gives rather abstract interface of GUI applications to script programs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: CTRON extended OS application to a gateway system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 11th TRON project International Symposium
abstract: CTRON-specification Extended OS programs for general file management, general program management, process management, and communication control (OSI and TCP/IP protocols) have been applied to a gateway system. This gateway system performs system interconnection and data conversion processing on a network linking various database systems. Features of the gateway are its facilitation of communication among a large number of different systems, its support of multiple protocols, and large-capacity file support for temporary storing of data. The Extended OS programs applied to the gateway were developed originally for another system and ported to this system. This paper reports on the applicability and portability of the CTRON-specification Extended OS to a gateway system. The analysis of portability examines the scale of modifications and the porting man-hours.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Eunice/ITRON: a control system development environment for ITRON machines
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 11th TRON project International Symposium
abstract: Eunice/ITRON is a control system development environment, whose target machines are ITRON machines. The core of Eunice/ITRON is a "full-lifecycle-support" language Nike. In Eunice/ITRON, except final performance tuning, development from abstract description level through semi-implementation level can be done on utilities-rich UNIX workstations. This way rapid and efficient development of control systems is attained. Nike is a concurrent object-oriented language. Dynamic behavior of each object can be described in state-transition model. In addition, to let the development process go forward and backward seamlessly, Nike provides refinement mechanism regarding states and their transitions, which can be validated at run-time. It not only conduces early executability, but also is the major driving force of refinement. Our implementation of the Nike compiler on an ITRON2-compliant operating system is discussed; and also that of Nikechat, a graphical executor under the X Window, of the system specified in Nike.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Performance analysis of communication control programs based on CTRON interfaces
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 11th TRON project International Symposium
abstract: The CTRON communication control interface specifications, based on OSI, define as system calls the functions to be provided to upper layers by the protocol processing at each layer. The authors discuss the implementation of communication control programs based on these interface specifications, noting the overhead factors involved in realizing a layered protocol, and suggesting ways of speeding up the protocol processing software.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A benchmark program and normalization method for evaluating communication systems-oriented realtime OS performance
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 11th TRON project International Symposium
abstract: This paper proposes a performance evaluation method, a benchmark program for Realtime Operating Systems and a normalization method for comparing the performance evaluation data between different processors. The benchmark program method is a traditional evaluation method for a processor and its compiler. However, there is no application for Realtime Operating System under Super multiple resource conditions. The authors propose a new algorithm for measuring all system call processing time of realtime operating systems under super multiple resource conditions. They also propose a new normalization method for comparing the OS performance between different processors. In this paper, the requirements of benchmark program and normalization program, the algorithm of benchmark program, examples of measuring data by new benchmark program and examples of normalization are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 11th TRON project International Symposium
abstract: Activities of the TRON Project in these past ten years have produced a large amount of technical results which are published as papers, books, and reports. Because such publications of TRON are scattered among diverse journals, proceedings, technical reports, etc., it is difficult for the new TRON researchers and developers to discover relevant documents. The primary objective of this bibliography is to eliminate this difficulty, and to improve the accessibility of technical information of the TRON Project. Its contents are restricted to publications on technical issues; nontechnical publications are out of its scope. At present, the bibliography contains more than 550 entries. Entries in this bibliography are classified into ten sections by their interests: books on the TRON Projects, Specifications, and technical papers on general issues, on TRON Specification CHIP, on ITRON, on CTRON, on BTRON, on HMI, on MTRON/HFDS, and on Enableware, In each section, entries are first sorted in the order of publishing year. Next, entries with the same publishing year are sorted in the alphabetical order of their authors' names.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
